issues.legal_issue: A person acting in private defence does not exceed that right when, in the circumstances, a real and imminent threat reasonably creates apprehension of death or grievous hurt and the force used is no more than necessary to meet it.
material_facts: The trial court acquitted the accused, finding that the prosecution had not proved beyond reasonable doubt that he was the aggressor; the High Court accepted that the other person was the aggressor but convicted the accused on the ground that he had exceeded his right of private defence.
The brothers had a history of bitter disputes and quarrels, and the evidence supported the finding that the deceased was the aggressor.

The deceased stooped to pick up a stone of a dangerous size. The eyewitness had not seen the accused draw his knife, and the evidence did not establish that the deceased stooped only after seeing the accused advance with the knife.
The Court found that the accused reasonably apprehended death or grievous hurt from a real and immediate danger and acted to ward it off without inflicting more harm than was necessary.
issues.conclusion: The accused acted within his right of private defence and did not exceed it. The High Court erred in convicting him; the appeal was allowed and the acquittal restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under the fourth clause of Section 99 of the Indian Penal Code, no more harm may be inflicted than is necessary for the purpose of defence. The right requires a reasonable apprehension of danger to the body from an attempt or threat to commit an offence, and does not arise until that apprehension exists. Whether the force used exceeded the right is a question of fact assessed objectively from the events and surrounding circumstances at the crucial time; no fixed pattern of conduct can be required. Once circumstances show an apprehension of death or grievous hurt, the defender may meet the threat, subject to the limit on necessary harm. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_conviction_after_acquittal and attacker_was_aggressor and attacker_reached_for_dangerous_object and defender_reasonably_apprehended_death_or_grievous_hurt and danger_was_real_and_imminent and defensive_force_not_more_than_necessary

predicates.appeal_from_conviction_after_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal from a conviction entered after a trial court acquitted the accused.
predicates.attacker_was_aggressor: The person posing the threat initiated or was the aggressor in the confrontation.
predicates.attacker_reached_for_dangerous_object: The aggressor reached for or picked up an object capable of causing serious harm.
predicates.defender_reasonably_apprehended_death_or: In the surrounding circumstances, the defender reasonably apprehended death or grievous hurt.
predicates.danger_was_real_and_imminent: The threat to the defender was real and immediate when the defensive act occurred.
predicates.defensive_force_not_more_than_necessary: The defender used no more force than was necessary to ward off the threat.

issues.definition: When an appeal follows a conviction replacing an acquittal, and the aggressor's immediate conduct created a reasonable apprehension of death or grievous hurt that was met with no more than necessary force, the acquittal is restored.
